title: System event detection system and method

source_provenance.note: Ephemeral request-token parameters are intentionally not persisted.

classification_signals: G06F21/552 long-term intrusion monitoring or reporting
G06F21/554 event detection and countermeasure context
H04L63/1425 traffic logging and anomaly detection
publicly_described_functional_concepts: receiving event records from system logs or security-monitoring applications
normalizing event records into event descriptor objects with structured properties
normalizing security-relevant entities into entity descriptor objects
linking events and entities in an object graph for cybersecurity analysis
using source-reliability signals when selecting entity-property values from multiple sources
deriving cybersecurity indicators from graph relationships
presenting linked events, entities, risks, vulnerabilities, indicators, sightings, observed data, reports, and defensive course-of-action objects to analysts
supporting graph traversal from a suspicious event to related entities and defensive response guidance

scope_model.analysis_loop: ingest authorized security events and entity context -> normalize descriptors -> resolve source reliability -> associate descriptors in graph -> derive indicators and risk context -> present linked evidence to analyst -> propose defensive course of action -> require policy/human approval before consequential action -> record provenance and outcome
building_patterns_relevant_to_independen: treat normalized event and entity descriptors as typed ontology objects rather than raw log strings
preserve source provenance and reliability alongside every normalized property
separate evidence objects from inferred indicators and risk objects
make every graph edge explainable through source properties or deterministic correlation rules
represent defensive response guidance as proposals, not automatic execution
require explicit approval before disruptive actions such as isolation, permission revocation, or deletion
provide reversible graph traversal from an alert back to source events and forward to related entities
use least-privilege connectors for logs, SIEM, identity, asset, and vulnerability systems
retain analyst decisions and response outcomes as feedback for later quality evaluation
keep automated containment disabled by default in the generic building profile

independent_claim_themes: display of event descriptor objects and retrieval of associated entity or defensive course-of-action objects through an object graph
event descriptors generated from system logs or security-monitoring applications
graph paths connecting security events, entities, and course-of-action descriptors
entity properties aggregated from multiple sources with reliability-aware selection
analysis of graph relationships to derive cybersecurity indicators

design_divergence_defaults: use independently designed event/entity schemas and graph edge semantics
store evidence, inference, and response-proposal objects in separate layers
use deterministic provenance and confidence fields on every normalization and correlation step
keep disruptive remediation out of the default automated path
require human approval and policy checks before containment or destructive actions
maintain complete event-to-source and response-to-outcome auditability

mandatory_safety_boundaries: no automatic disruptive remediation by default
human approval for containment or destructive actions
